subject: Coffee & Tea
title: The Adenosine Trick
description: A 60-second lesson on The Adenosine Trick.

hook.text: Caffeine doesn't give you energy. It blocks the brain chemical that tells you you're tired.

buildup.text: Adenosine is a molecule that builds up in your brain throughout the day, making you progressively sleepier.

discovery.text: Caffeine's molecular shape is almost identical to adenosine. It fits into the same receptors—but doesn't activate them.

twist.text: With receptors blocked, adenosine can't deliver its 'time to sleep' signal—so you feel alert even when you're tired.

climax.text: Caffeine doesn't create wakefulness. It silences sleepiness. The tiredness is still there, just hidden.

punchline.text: Not an energy boost—a tiredness blocker. Caffeine is a disguise.

quiz.question: How does caffeine make you feel alert?
options: It blocks adenosine receptors that signal tiredness
